title: Embedded Figures
summary: Find a small figure hidden inside a bigger one exactly as drawn — same size and orientation (rotation is not allowed). Anchor on the most distinctive stroke, usually a slant, and reject options that are flips or rotations of the true part.

subtopics.title: Finding the hidden part in a figure
subtopics.concept:
A big figure hides one of the small option figures. The hidden figure has the same strokes, the same lengths and the same directions. Your job is to find which option it is.

You may slide the small figure around. You may **not** turn it or flip it.

tricks.title: Reject by a missing direction
tricks.body: Look at which slants the big figure has. An option with a slant the figure lacks cannot be hidden in it.

example.q: The big figure has only rising slants (`/`). An option has one falling slant (`\`). Can that option be hidden in it?
steps: The figure has no `\` stroke anywhere.
Sliding cannot change a `\` into a `/`.
So the option cannot fit.

tricks.title: Count strokes by type
tricks.body: Count the flat, upright and slanting strokes in the part. The big figure must have at least as many of each type.

example.q: An option has 3 flat strokes in a row. The big figure has only 2 flat strokes in each row. Can it be hidden?
steps: A row of 3 flat strokes needs 3 flat strokes in one line.
No line in the figure has 3.
So the option cannot fit.

tricks.title: Two finalists: compare at the anchor
tricks.body: If two options look alike, compare only the strokes that touch the anchor. The wrong one usually breaks there.

mistakes.wrong: Choosing an option because the overall shape looks right.
mistakes.right: Check every stroke and its direction. Shape alone hides flips and turns.

mistakes.wrong: Accepting a turned or mirrored copy.
mistakes.right: Rotation is not allowed. A `/` slant in the figure never matches a `\` slant in the option.

mistakes.wrong: Accepting an option that misses one stroke, or has one stroke in another direction.
mistakes.right: Every stroke of the option must be present. One missing or re-angled stroke means reject.

mistakes.wrong: Checking only the first place where the anchor stroke appears.
mistakes.right: Try every place where the anchor appears before you reject an option.
All strokes are one square long here. Size never decides. Direction does.

subtopics.notes:
### What hidden means
One small figure sits inside the big figure. Extra lines are drawn around it to hide it.

The four options are small figures. Pick the option that appears **exactly** inside the big one.

> **Rule:** Sliding is allowed. Turning and flipping are not allowed.

### How the pictures look here
The exam shows drawings. We draw them with text.

- `+` is a corner point. `.` is an empty point.
- `-` is a flat stroke. `|` is an upright stroke.
- `/` is a rising slant. `\` is a falling slant. `X` means both slants cross in that square.

Every stroke is one square long. So the size of a stroke never decides the answer.

### Flips and turns are wrong answers
Most wrong options are copies of the right answer with one simple change.

| Copy | What changes | Allowed? |
|---|---|---|
| Mirror image | Left and right swap | No |
| Water image | Top and bottom swap | No |
| Turned copy | Turned by 90 or 180 degrees | No |

A `/` slant becomes a `\` slant in a mirror image. So check the slants first.

### Pick a rare stroke first
Do not compare whole figures. Pick **one stroke** that is rare in the small figure. A slant is the best choice.

1. Find that stroke in the big figure. Match its direction.
2. Check the strokes that touch it. Are they there too?
3. Trace the other strokes one by one.
4. If one stroke is missing, drop that place and try the next one.

> **Tip:** A flat or upright stroke appears many times. A slant appears only a few times. Fewer places means less work.

### Count strokes by type
Count the part's strokes: flat, upright, rising slant and falling slant. The big figure must have **at least** that many of each type.

If the part has a `\` slant and the big figure has none, that option is out. You do not need to trace anything.

> **Watch:** Two options can have the same number of strokes and still differ in direction.

### A worked example
Which option is hidden in the given figure? Rotation is not allowed.

**Figure**
```
+   +   +---+
| /
+   +   .   +
      \   /
+---+---+   .
```

**(A)**
```
+   .   .   .
  \
.   +---+---+
```

**(B)**
```
.   .   .   +
          /
+---+---+   .
```

**(C)**
```
+   .   .   +
  \       /
.   +---+   .
```

**Solution**
- Part strokes: 2 flat and 1 rising slant (`/`).
- Anchor on the rising slant (`/`). The figure has 2 of them.
- (A) is the mirror image (left and right swapped), so it does not fit anywhere.
- (C) has one stroke changed, so it does not fit anywhere.
- Only (B) fits, in the bottom part of the figure.

Answer: **(B)**.

subtopics.title: Which figure contains the given part
subtopics.concept:
This is the reverse question. One small part is given, and each option is a bigger figure. Choose the option that contains the part **exactly as drawn**.

Extra lines never matter. You may slide the part but not turn it or flip it.

tricks.title: Reject by a missing direction
tricks.body: List the directions in the part: flat, upright, `/` and `\`. An option that lacks one of them is out at once.

example.q: The part has a flat stroke, an upright stroke and a falling slant (`\`). Option B has no falling slant at all. Keep B?
steps: The part needs a `\` stroke.
Option B has none.
Sliding cannot create one.

tricks.title: Count the strokes first
tricks.body: The option must have at least as many strokes as the part. Fewer strokes means it cannot contain the part.

example.q: The part has 5 strokes. Option C has 4 strokes in total. Can C contain the part?
steps: A figure with 4 strokes cannot hold 5 strokes.
So C cannot contain the part.

tricks.body: If two options survive, compare only the strokes that touch the anchor. The wrong one usually breaks a stroke there.

subtopics.notes:
### The task
A small **part** is given. Each option is a bigger figure. Exactly one option contains the part. It has the same strokes, lengths and directions.

The option may have extra strokes around the part. That is fine.

> **Rule:** The part must be present in full. Extra lines never disqualify an option.

### Read the pictures
- `+` is a corner point. `.` is an empty point.
- `-` is a flat stroke. `|` is an upright stroke.
- `/` is a rising slant. `\` is a falling slant. `X` means both slants cross in that square.

Every stroke is one square long.

### List the part's strokes
Write down the strokes with their directions. For example: 2 flat, 1 upright, 1 rising slant.

The right option shows all of them, joined in the same way. Sliding is allowed. Turning is not.

### Use a rare stroke as anchor
A slant is rarer than a flat or upright stroke. Start with it.

1. Check its lean: `/` rises to the right, `\` falls to the right.
2. Find it in the option.
3. Check the strokes that touch it, one by one.
4. Also try a **T-joint**: one stroke that ends on the middle of another. It is the next best anchor.

> **Tip:** Parts often sit against an edge or in a corner of the correct option. Scan the border first.

### Near-miss options
Wrong options are usually one step away from the part. One stroke is **missing**, **changed** or **turned**.

Counting strokes is not enough. A wrong option can have the same number of strokes as the part.

> **Watch:** Check each stroke's direction and its end points. They must match the part.

### A good scan order
Do the same steps for every option. This keeps you fast and calm.

1. Count the strokes. Drop any option with fewer strokes than the part.
2. Check the directions. Drop any option that lacks a direction the part needs.
3. Trace the anchor stroke and its neighbours in each option that is left.
4. Choose the option where every stroke lines up.

Most questions end after step 2 or 3. You rarely need to trace all four options in full.

### A worked example
Which option contains the given part exactly as drawn? Rotation is not allowed.

**Part**
```
+   .   +
|     /
+---+---+
```

**(A)**
```
+---+   +   .
  \     |
+---+---+---+

.   +---+   .
```

**(B)**
```
+   .   +
|     /
+   +   +
| \   /
+---+---+
```

**(C)**
```
.   +---+   +
      \   /
.   +   +   .
  /   /
+---+---+   .
```

**Solution**
- Part strokes: 2 flat, 1 upright and 1 rising slant (`/`).
- Anchor on the rising slant (`/`) and trace the other strokes around it.
- (A) only has a mirror-image copy, so the part is not there.
- (C) only has a copy with one stroke changed, so the part is not there.
- (B) holds the part in the bottom part of the option.

Answer: **(B)**.
